title: Types of Products Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 15
description:
Mrs. Rao buys her Laddoo Lab six-pack every week without a second thought, but for her daughter's school bag she visited four shops and compared every zip. Same customer, two very different ways of buying. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab to understand product classification: sorting products by how and why people buy them.

You will see how Melvin Copeland of Harvard sorted consumer goods into convenience, shopping and specialty goods in 1923, why textbooks add a fourth type, unsought products, and the second family of industrial products. Then we watch four of Mrs. Rao's purchases (a six-pack, a school bag, a silk saree and life insurance) travel through three simple questions into four bins, and see what each type means for marketing. Laddoo Lab turns buyer too: ragi and jaggery are materials, the grinder is a capital item, and tape and gas are supplies. We see the four types at work today in a biscuit maker, a phone maker, a luxury watchmaker and an insurer, and end honestly: the same product can sit in different boxes for different buyers.

This is Episode 15 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
